newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: French Guiana mob linked to murder attempt.
newsitem.headline: French Guiana mob linked to murder attempt.

text.p: Ten people, including four leading members of French Guiana's independence movement, allegedly set fire to a state prosecutor's house while he and his family were asleep, a prosecutor handling the case said on Tuesday.

Yves Charpenel, head prosecutor of the appeals court of Fort-de-France in French Caribbean island of Martinique said the attack against French Guiana's state prosecutor Jean-Luc Beck during riots last November constituted attempted murder.
The 10 were transferred to Martinique last week and charged with arson and violence against a magistrate. Their arrests have triggered a new wave of riots in French Guiana's capital of Cayenne.

More than 1,000 demonstrators marched through central Cayenne on Tuesday chanting "liberate our comrades." A general strike closed numerous government services and Air France was forced to delay a flight to Paris by 24 hours.
Charpenel has been given jurisdication of the case since French law prohibits a magistrate personally involved in an incident to proceed with prosecution
Charpenel told a news conference that while police were busy combating looters in a commercial section of Cayenne in November, Beck's house was chosen for attack.

"In another section of town, the section where the prosecutors house is located, he (Beck) is asleep with his family at 2.30 a.m. in the morning. Between 20 and 30 people arrive, set the house on fire. Hear the cries of women and children. Stop and go out to get more gasoline, since they had run out of gasoline. Came back and relit the house on fire. They were dispersed only by the arrival of police, " he said.
Three nights of rioting in the last two weeks have left 11 police wounded including 10 by gunfire.
Last week four of the accused had to be transfered to Martinique aboard a French naval vessel since demonstrators blocked access to Cayenne's airport.
The city is tense and patrolled by hundreds of paramilitary riot police reinforcements flown in from mainland France last week.

French Guiana is the only non-independent territory on the mainland of the Western Hemisphere. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
